Dania's baby son was on her lap when he was shot by the IDF. “I loved him so much. I’d always wanted children and he was the life of our house,” says Dania Salameh, 28, sitting in her spotless flat on the outskirts of Bethlehem with her husband, Fahd Abu Haikal, 41. He teaches media and graphic design at the city’s Ahliya University, where they met. A photograph near the TV shows them both in robes at a graduation ceremony before they married two years ago. “They killed my baby son in cold blood,” says Abu Haikal, his voice tight with anger. “We were just a family in a car on a Friday afternoon.” Sam is one of 259 Palestinian children killed on the West Bank since Israel launched military operations in response to the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023, according to the United Nations — almost two a week. Overall, more than 1,100 Palestinians and 40 Israelis have been killed in the West Bank, according to the United Nations Office for the Co-ordination of Humanitarian Affairs. “I cry every day,” Salameh says. “Sam was so calm and happy, always smiling… Now the flat is very quiet and my heart is broken.” #westbank #idf #bethlehem #palestine #israel
